name: Champagne Toast
description: A bottle with the cork flying out paired with two glasses clinking together. This is the full picture of celebration — the moment something pops and two people raise their glasses to it together.
meaning: 🍾🥂 means 'let's celebrate this together.' The bottle captures the big moment (the news, the win, the announcement), and the clinking glasses turn it into a shared experience. Together they say 'this is worth marking, and I want to do it with you.'
examples: to us and everything we built this year 🍾🥂
seoDescription: What does 🍾🥂 mean? It's celebration with company — a bottle popping with news paired with clinking glasses to share the moment together.

longForm.overview:
🍾🥂 is celebration with company. The bottle alone says 'something big happened' — a promotion, an engagement, a deadline met, a relationship milestone. The clinking glasses add a second voice: 'and I want to toast it with you.' The combo works because it combines announcement with invitation. You are not just sharing news; you are saying 'this moment includes you.'

The two emojis do distinct work. 🍾 is the event itself — the cork pops, something genuinely shifted. 🥂 is the togetherness — it is two glasses, not one, which means the sender is marking the moment as something shared rather than personal. This is what separates 🍾🥂 from sending 🍾 alone. A single bottle can feel like bragging. The clinking glasses reframe it as 'we did this' or 'let's acknowledge this together,' which softens the tone and deepens the intimacy.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🍾🥂 lives in close conversations — group chats between friends, messages to a partner, tight team channels at work. It shows up when someone has news they want to celebrate but also want to share the moment with the person reading it. The combo is frequent on relationship milestones (anniversaries, moving in together, engagements), work wins (project shipped, promotion, contract signed), and life achievements (graduated, got the job, survived the semester).

In dating it often reads as 'we have something worth celebrating,' which carries real weight. In friend groups it is the response to 'guess what' when the answer is good news. At work it shows up in smaller channels where the team already knows each other well — it would feel out of place in a company-wide announcement, but perfect in a Slack thread celebrating a ship.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🍾🥂 when the celebration is one-sided or the news is not yet public. If someone shared something they are still processing or keeping quiet, responding with 🍾🥂 can feel like you are pressuring them to party before they are ready. Avoid it when the moment is bittersweet — a job change that involves leaving people behind, a move that mixes excitement with loss. The combo is pure celebration and will read as tone deaf if there is complicated emotion in the mix.

Also avoid 🍾🥂 in formal or professional settings with people you do not know well. A single 🥂 or a written 'congratulations' lands better in a wider org channel. Save the full combo for circles where your warmth and excitement will read as genuine rather than performative.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends you 🍾🥂 on your good news, mirror it back — 🍾🥂 on its own says 'thank you, let's keep this going.' If you want to escalate the warmth, add a sentence that names what you are actually celebrating: 'to you finally getting the yes 🍾🥂' or 'so proud of you for taking the leap 🍾🥂.' This lands as more sincere than the emoji alone.

If you are celebrating someone else's moment and want your reply to stand out, pair the combo with a specific memory or detail: 'remember when you said you wanted this job? 🍾🥂' A reply that shows you were paying attention reads as more meaningful than just matching their energy. If the moment warrants it, a 😭🥂 (moved to tears, cheering together) signals that the news actually moved you, which often reads as the highest compliment you can give.

faqs.question: What does 🍾🥂 mean in a group chat
faqs.answer: It means someone is celebrating something and wants everyone in the chat to celebrate with them. It is an invitation to acknowledge a win together. The person sending it usually expects replies of the same energy — matching emojis or congratulations.

faqs.question: Is 🍾🥂 flirty
faqs.answer: It can be in dating contexts, especially around anniversaries or relationship milestones. 'Happy one year 🍾🥂' or 'to us' paired with the combo reads as romantic and intimate. In other contexts it is just celebratory, not flirty.

faqs.question: Can I send 🍾🥂 if I am not actually celebrating with someone
faqs.answer: Not really — the clinking glasses are specifically about togetherness, so sending it to someone you are not actually with or not actually close to will read as hollow. Send 🍾 alone if you just want to celebrate their news from a distance.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🍾🥂 and 🎉🙌
faqs.answer: 🍾🥂 is intimate and specific — it is about celebrating with someone you are already close to. 🎉🙌 is louder and more general — it works for any big win and does not require the same relationship closeness. Use 🍾🥂 for moments you want to feel personal and shared.

conversationExamples.message: three years today 🍾🥂 can't wait to celebrate tonight
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are marking an anniversary and want to make the evening feel special and shared. This is romantic without being over the top. Respond with matching warmth: 'love you, can't wait 🍾🥂' or a specific detail about your plans together.

conversationExamples.message: got the internship offer 🍾🥂 we have to go out this weekend
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are excited about their win and want to celebrate it with you in person. The combo says 'this is big enough to mark with you.' Respond enthusiastically and confirm plans: 'YES let's go 🍾🥂' or 'i'm so proud of you, when are you free.'

conversationExamples.message: shipped it to production 🍾🥂 thanks for all the debugging help
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are celebrating a team win and giving you credit for being part of it. This is warm but professional. Respond with 'let's celebrate this one 🍾🥂' or 'great work getting it live.'

conversationExamples.message: mom and dad got engaged 🍾🥂 we're all going out to dinner tonight
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are sharing big family news and want to celebrate it as a family unit. The combo frames the moment as something everyone will experience together. Respond with genuine excitement: 'oh my god congratulations to them 🍾🥂' or ask for details.

conversationExamples.message: album dropped today 🍾🥂 thank you all for waiting
conversationExamples.interpretation: A creator is celebrating a release milestone with their audience and thanking them for being part of the moment. The combo is inclusive — it says 'we got here together.' Respond with enthusiasm and maybe a reaction to the work itself.
